items.excerpt: Kickstarter rejected her product, but she built the same product into a million-dollar brand. Learn how viral videos and founder-led content transformed an overlooked pain point into success.
items.body: Kickstarter rejected her product, but she built the same product into a million-dollar brand. Learn how viral videos and founder-led content transformed an overlooked pain point into success. ► Watch the podcasts on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@Helium10SeriousSellersPodcast?sub_confirmation=1 ► Instagram: instagram.com/serioussellerspodcast ► Free Amazon Seller Chrome Extension: https://h10.me/extension ► Sign Up For Helium 10: https://h10.me/signup (Use SSP10 To Save 10% For Life) ► Learn How to Sell on Amazon: https://h10.me/ft What happens when a failed nursing student, experienced e-commerce marketer, and new mother transforms a personal frustration into a million-dollar brand? In this episode, Bradley Sutton speaks with Kate Bray, founder of Reb Relief, about the unconventional journey that led her from Amazon advertising and agency leadership to creating a product inspired by her postpartum experience. After building and testing her own prototype, Kate posted a seven-second TikTok video that went viral and a second video helped her collect approximately 1,500 email sign-ups before producing a single unit. Her launch nearly collapsed when Kickstarter rejected the product just three days before the campaign was scheduled to begin. Instead of walking away, Kate turned the rejection into a powerful marketing hook and moved the launch to Shopify. Through preorders, a local credit-union loan, and investments from strategic advisors, she raised enough to fund a $60,000 initial purchase order. Despite spending most of her career in the Amazon ecosystem, Kate has yet to launch Reb Relief on Amazon because the brand has remained consistently sold out through Shopify. items.title: SP-API Release Notes
items.excerpt: Selling Partner API new features, software updates, and changelog.
items.body: For releases prior to January 19, 2022, refer to Announcements in the Selling Partner API GitHub repo . August 26, 2026 API changes Promotions API v2025-12-01 Launched the new Promotions API, which you can use to search, retrieve, and manage promotions. The Promotions API supports multiple promotion types: deals, coupons, price discounts, and basket building promotions. You can use it to programmatically monitor promotion status, review item selections, and identify validation issues. Reports v2021-06-30 Added the promotionsApiMappingId field to the GET_COUPON_PERFORMANCE_REPORT and GET_PROMOTION_PERFORMANCE_REPORT report types. Sellers and vendors can use this field to cross-reference performance report data with promotions managed through the Promotions API . Documentation changes Added the Seller Authorizations FAQ . Updated the Security and Compliance Best Practices Guide to reflect new and revised requirements in the Data Protection Policy (DPP), Acceptable Use Policy (AUP), and Solution Provider Portal Agreement. Deprecation notices Deprecated SP-API resources are no longer in active development. Calls to deprecated SP-API resources will fail as of their removal date. For a complete list of SP-API deprecations, refer to the SP-API Deprecation Schedule . August 5, 2026 API changes Tracking API v2026-01-30 Launched the new Tracking API with one operation available in the US store. The getShipmentTracking operation allows sellers and vendors to retrieve tracking details for a shipment as it moves through Amazon’s supply chain. For more information, refer to Tracking API . Notifications V1 Launched the SHIPMENT_TRACKING_MILESTONE_CHANGED notification type. Sellers and vendors can subscribe to this notification type to receive real-time tracking updates for a shipment...

items.title: #764 - TikTok, AI, and a $3M Soap Brand
items.excerpt: What do homemade soap, TikTok creators, AI automation, and old-school catalogs have in common? Discover how two sellers use them to build and grow multimillion-dollar e-commerce brands.
items.body: What do homemade soap, TikTok creators, AI automation, and old-school catalogs have in common? Discover how two sellers use them to build and grow multimillion-dollar e-commerce brands. ► Watch the podcasts on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@Helium10SeriousSellersPodcast?sub_confirmation=1 ► Instagram: instagram.com/serioussellerspodcast ► Free Amazon Seller Chrome Extension: https://h10.me/extension ► Sign Up For Helium 10: https://h10.me/signup (Use SSP10 To Save 10% For Life) ► Learn How To Sell on Amazon: https://h10.me/ft What does it take to turn a homemade product into a multimillion-dollar brand? In this episode, Bradley Sutton speaks with Joe McCutcheon, founder of Carolina Castile Soap, and Marc Messer from Advanced Bionutritionals. Together, they reveal how product differentiation, creator partnerships, AI-powered systems, and even old-school direct mail can produce remarkable results in today’s e-commerce world. Joe began making soap for his cleaning company before testing it on eBay and eventually launching on Amazon. After years of reinvesting his profits and producing batches from his kitchen and garage, he grew Carolina Castile Soap from $1.8 million last year toward a projected $3 million this year. Joe explains how professional packaging, distinctive scents, Helium 10 research, and a community of TikTok creators helped the brand stand apart. Today, approximately 70% of its revenue comes from Amazon, while TikTok Shop has become both a profitable channel and a source of additional Amazon demand. Marc shares a very different path to growth at Advanced Bionutritionals, a primarily direct-to-consumer company generating between $30 million and $50 million annually.
